title: Sapiensly App Manifest v1
description: The App manifest schema: objects (the data model — fields including formula/lookup/rollup, file, rich_text and relations), pages (with interactive blocks: form, table, button, modal, chart, kanban, calendar, tabs and more), workflows (triggers + steps), permissions, settings and an optional agent.

agent.description: Optional embedded runtime agent (builder power #3). End-users of the app instruct it; its toolset is auto-derived from the capabilities granted here. Reads run live; every write is propose-don't-mutate (gated, slice 2). Absent ⇒ no agent.

enabled.description: Whether the runtime agent is served for this app.

instructions.description: Runtime system prompt — how the assistant should behave.

capabilities.description: Which manifest capabilities the agent may use. Absent grant ⇒ none (fail-closed). The agent can never exceed what is granted here.

read.description: Objects the agent may read: "all" or an explicit list of object ids.

write.description: Objects the agent may PROPOSE writes against (executed only via the gate, slice 2): "all" or an explicit list. Empty ⇒ read-only agent (safest default).

autonomy.description: Master switch. "propose" (default): every write is human-approved. "safe": the autonomy engine honors the per-capability `safe` marks below — only those actions auto-execute; everything else stays gated (fail-closed).

safe.description: Per-capability auto-execute marks (honored only when autonomy="safe"). An object entry lets the agent run create/update on that object WITHOUT approval; a workflow entry lets it run that workflow without approval. Hard limits: only internal objects auto-execute (connected writes are always gated), only create/update for objects (delete is never auto-executable — note the actions enum), and a workflow auto-runs only when explicitly listed.

id.description: Prefixed identifier: a short lowercase tag (2-5 chars) + underscore + 3-60 alphanumeric/underscore chars. A standard ULID (26 chars) fits comfortably, but a short readable token works too (e.g. kpi_otd001, blk_p1hero). The runtime treats the value as opaque after the validator accepts it; uniqueness in scope is checked separately. The sys_ namespace is reserved for system virtual fields (sys_created_at, sys_updated_at).

col_span.description: Relative column WIDTH weight when this block is a direct child of a `direction:"row"` container. Children split the row width by their weights (all columns stay the same HEIGHT). E.g. a wide chart with col_span 7 next to a companion with col_span 3 → 70/30. Give every child of the row a col_span, or none (unset = equal columns). Ignored outside a row.

full_bleed.description: Make the section span the full content width (edge to edge) instead of sitting inside the page padding. Use on top-level coloured sections.

gradient.description: Linear-gradient background (overrides `background`). Keep `from`/`to` in the same tonal range so the auto-contrast text colour reads against both ends. A stop may be a literal hex, or a palette ramp variable WITH a hex fallback — `var(--sp-accent-900, #003961)` — which keeps the gradient live: it follows the app's accent and `palette_mode` (e.g. "grays") instead of freezing the colour that was active when the block was authored.

min_height.description: Minimum block height in px — the manual-adjust resize writes it; the renderer applies it as min-height.

source_definition.description: Backing store for an object. Absent or {type:internal} = the records store (default). {type:connected} = an external system reached through an integration (connected object).

integration_id.description: The authorized integration this object reads/writes through.

id_path.description: Dot path to the external record id within a row.

operations.description: Maps each CRUD operation to an external request. Omit create/update for a read-only connected object.

field_map.description: Ties manifest fields to external response paths. Partial-tolerant: unmapped fields render null.

source_operation.description: One external operation for a connected object. EITHER a REST request (method+path, with optional paging/sort/filter param mappings) OR an MCP tool call (mcp_tool + optional static arguments) — the bound integration's transport decides which. Either way the returned JSON rows are mapped by the object's field_map/id_path.

path.description: Path appended to the integration base URL; may template {id}. REST only.

mcp_tool.description: For an MCP integration: the name of the tool to call for this operation (e.g. a list/query tool). Its returned JSON rows feed field_map/id_path. Use instead of method+path.

arguments.description: Static arguments passed to the MCP tool call (e.g. a page size). MCP only.

collection_path.description: Dot path to the row array in a list response (e.g. "results"). Works for REST and MCP results alike.

page_param.description: Query param name for pagination, when supported.

page_mode.description: How page_param is expressed: a raw offset (default) or a 1-based page number derived from offset/limit.

page_size_param.description: Query param name for the page size (the query's limit), when supported.

sort_param.description: Query param name to sort by; its value is the sort field's external_path.

order_param.description: Optional query param name for the sort direction (asc/desc).

filter_params.description: Pushes simple equality filters down to external query params. Non-equality conditions degrade gracefully (not pushed down).

capture.description: Where the value comes FROM. Omit for an ordinary text box. Every one of these is an EXTRA way in — the box still accepts a typed value, on a desktop, with the hardware missing or with permission refused, so the field is never a dead end, and the VALUE is a plain string either way so filters, tables and exports need no special handling. `barcode` adds a Scan button that reads a barcode or QR with the camera, and makes the field recognise a handheld scanner gun (which types the code and sends Enter) so the operator never touches the screen — SKUs, asset tags, tracking numbers, batch and serial numbers. `nfc` reads a tag held against the phone (Chrome on Android only): its text or url payload, or failing that the tag's own serial number — access cards, asset tags glued to a machine, anything with no room for a printed label. `contact` opens the phone's contact picker and takes the person's name — use it on the email and phone types too, where it takes their address and number instead. `dictation` adds a microphone that types what is said into the box, using the browser's own recogniser rather than a model, so it costs nothing and works while the person's hands are full.

`contact` adds a button that opens the phone's own contact picker and fills in the address it finds. Chrome on Android only; everywhere else the box is a box. Use it wherever somebody is typing in details they already have in their phone.

allOf.description: An email address. Writes validate the format server-side; forms render an email input.
A web URL (http/https). Writes validate the format server-side; forms render a url input.

capture.description: `contact` adds a button that opens the phone's own contact picker and fills in the number it finds. Chrome on Android only; everywhere else the box is a box. Use it wherever somebody is typing in a number they already have in their phone.

allOf.description: A phone number (digits, spaces, +()-. allowed). Forms render a tel input.

capture.description: `dictation` adds a microphone that types what is said into the box, appending to whatever is already there. The browser's own recogniser, not a model — it costs nothing per use and needs no upload. Use it for the field somebody fills in standing next to the machine they are describing: findings, notes, what was done. The box stays a box, so a browser without a recogniser (Firefox, most of Safari) is simply a browser somebody types into.

`scale` adds a button that reads the number off a machine plugged into the computer — a shop scale, a caliper, a bench meter, nearly all of which send a line of text over a serial port several times a second. Somebody reading that display and typing it into the form is the step that puts the wrong weight on the invoice, and it is the step this removes. It waits for two agreeing readings and refuses one the device marks as unsettled, so a pan still moving is never written down. Chromium only, and it needs somebody to point at the port — so the box beside it still takes a typed number, which is what happens everywhere else.

display.description: How the form renders it: a checkbox (default) or a toggle switch.
How the form renders it: a dropdown (default) or a radio group — radio is nicer for 2-5 always-visible options.

items.description: A select option. Required keys: `id` (id-pattern), `value` (the stored slug-like string you pass to actions/seed_records — NOT `slug`), and `label` (the human display text). Optional `color` (#RRGGBB chip).

A select option. Required keys: `id` (id-pattern), `value` (the stored slug-like string you pass to actions/seed_records — NOT `slug`), and `label` (the human display text). Optional `color` (#RRGGBB chip).

max_length.description: Maximum length of the plain-text content (HTML tags excluded).

mime_types.description: Optional MIME allowlist. Accepts wildcards like image/*. When omitted, any MIME is allowed (subject to the global size limit).

capture.description: Where the file comes FROM. Omit for the ordinary file picker. `camera` asks the device for a photo: on a phone or tablet it opens the camera directly, and on a desktop it falls back to the picker, so the field always works; implies an image/* accept unless mime_types says otherwise. Use it for damage reports, proof of delivery, meter readings and site inspections. `signature` replaces the picker with a pad the person signs on with a finger, a stylus or the mouse, and stores the result as a PNG — use it for delivery notes, consent, handover and inspection sign-off. `screenshot` asks the desktop for a picture of a window or a screen and stores that — for support tickets and bug reports, where what somebody is looking at IS the report and describing it in words is the step that loses the detail. All three store the SAME value as any file field, so tables, detail pages and exports need no special handling.

stamp.description: Only with capture:"camera". Takes the photo INSIDE the page instead of handing over to the phone's camera app, and burns the date, the time and the coordinates into the corner of the image before it is uploaded. Use it when the photo is EVIDENCE — a meter reading, damage on arrival, proof that somebody was where they say they were — because a plain photo proves what was in front of a lens and not when or where. The person is told what is being written, and refusing the location writes the time alone rather than failing. Costs the OS camera's focus and exposure, so leave it off for photos that are simply attachments.

field_geo.description: A point on the earth: {lat, lng} and, when the device reported one, {accuracy} in metres. Captured with a «use my location» button on the device, or typed in — both are always available, so the field works in an office as well as on a roof. Renders on the `map` block via geo_field_id. Use it for site visits, deliveries, asset locations, meter readings and inspections. NOTE: this stores where somebody CHOSE to record, not where they are; there is no automatic stamping, because tracking staff is a decision an app owner has to make deliberately and tell their people about.

capture.description: `auto` asks the device for the location as soon as the form opens, instead of waiting for somebody to press the button. Set it ONLY when the whole point of the field is where the person was — a visit check-in, proof of delivery — and never as a convenience, because a location taken without being asked for is the difference between recording work and tracking staff. The form SAYS it did it, in a line under the field, and every other way in stays: the coordinates can still be typed, picked on a map or replaced. A refusal is not an error; the field is simply empty and waiting, exactly as it would be without this.

field_definition.description: An object field. Its `type` must be one of the catalog types (string, email, url, phone, long_text, number, currency, boolean, date, datetime, single_select, multi_select, relation, formula, lookup, rollup, rating, slider, rich_text, file, date_range, color, geo). If this failed, the `type` is unknown or required props for that type are missing — call list_available_field_types. Derived types (formula/lookup/rollup) require readonly:true.

filter_expression.description: A filter is a single OBJECT (not an array). Either a leaf condition {op, field_id, value|value_expression} where op is eq|neq|gt|gte|lt|lte|in|not_in|contains|starts_with|ends_with|is_null|is_not_null|between — e.g. {"op":"eq","field_id":"fld_…","value":"activo"}; OR a group {op:"and"|"or", conditions:[…nested filters…]}; OR {op:"not", condition:{…}}; OR a relation traversal {op:"related", field_id:"<a relation field>", condition:{…filter on the RELATED object…}} — keeps rows whose related record(s) match (belongs_to and has_many). To combine several conditions wrap them in one and/or group, never pass a bare array.

oneOf.description: Relation traversal: keep rows whose related record(s) match the sub-condition. field_id must be a relation field on the queried object; condition is a filter over the RELATED object's fields.

field_condition.description: A single structured condition over another field of the SAME form, evaluated reactively against the live form values. Used by visible_if / required_if. `value` is a literal compared against the referenced field's current value (an array for in/not_in; omitted for is_null/is_not_null/is_truthy/is_falsy).

ratio_operand.description: Makes the KPI a RATIO: its value becomes (this block's aggregation of its query) ÷ (this denominator's aggregation). Use format=percentage for rates (win rate = won ÷ closed, conversion = converted ÷ total). The trend chip is omitted for ratios.

spark.description: Draws a small inline trend line (sparkline) inside the KPI card, beside its value — a compact history behind the single number. `data_source` is a query for the rows to plot; `x_field_id` (a date/datetime, bucketed by day) orders them and `y_field_id` + `aggregation` (default count) is the measure. Typically the same object as the KPI, scoped to the current period, e.g. the daily spend behind a 'Total spend' figure.

x_field_id.description: Date/datetime field the series is ordered/bucketed by (by day). Omit to plot rows in query order.

y_field_id.description: Numeric field to aggregate per bucket (omit for a count of rows).

color.description: Line colour; defaults to the brand accent.

search.description: Case-insensitive free-text match across the object's text fields (string, long_text, single_select, …). ANDed across whitespace-separated terms.

page.description: A page. Required keys: id, slug, name, `path` (the URL, e.g. "/clientes" — easy to forget) and `blocks` (an array, may be empty).

path.description: Required URL path for the page, e.g. "/clientes". Must start with "/" and contain only lowercase letters, digits, /, _, - or : (no spaces or uppercase). Typically "/" + the page slug.

keep_awake.description: Hold the screen on while this page is open. For a page worked ON rather than looked at: a scanning station, the till on a counter, an inspection form filled in over twenty minutes with gloves on. Per page and never per app — the app also has a list somebody leaves open on a desk. Silently does nothing where the browser has no Wake Lock API.

live.description: Refresh this block when somebody ELSE changes one of its records. The server broadcasts three ids and a verb — never the row — and the page re-reads through the ordinary access-filtered path, so nobody learns of a record they could not already open. One subscription per page however many blocks ask for it, and writes are coalesced, so a busy app costs one query rather than a queue of them. Use it for shared queues, dispatch boards and dashboards on a wall; leave it off for a form somebody is typing into.

content.description: Bespoke section markup — the landing design escape hatch that lets the model compose a page that isn't a recombination of fixed blocks. Author semantic HTML (section/div/span/headings/img/lists/tables) with `class`/`id`, then style it ENTIRELY through settings.custom_css: inline `style`, `<script>`, `<style>` and event handlers are stripped on save, so styling MUST live in custom_css. Opt into motion with data-sp-* hooks (e.g. data-sp-reveal, data-sp-motion="ambient-field") that the runtime hydrates — never author JavaScript. When the landing is multilingual this holds the DEFAULT language; the others go in content_i18n.

content_i18n.description: Translations of this section, keyed by language code (e.g. "es"). `content` is the DEFAULT language — the first entry of settings.languages — and these are the alternatives. A language with no entry falls back to `content`, so a partial translation degrades to the default instead of breaking. Every variant MUST keep the same structure as `content` (same elements, same order, same classes): only the words change. The design lives in custom_css and is shared, and gestures that address an element by position (the fine-tune Links panel) rely on the structures matching. Variants are sanitised on save exactly like `content`, and only the negotiated language is ever sent to the browser.

object_id.description: The object new leads are written into (e.g. a 'leads' object). Pair it with a record.created workflow on that object so every submission is handled by your agents.

fields.description: The inputs the visitor fills, mapped to fields of the lead object. ONLY these fields are accepted by the public endpoint — anything else is rejected.

input.description: The HTML input treatment; the stored value still validates against the object field's own type.

success_message.description: Shown in place of the form after a successful submission. Honest default: an agent is already on it.

direction.description: row = equal side-by-side columns (stretch to a shared height); column = stacked; masonry = pack children at their natural height into responsive columns, filling vertical gaps (for INDEPENDENT cards of varying height — reading order is column-major).

size.description: Visual size override, independent of the semantic `level`. Use `xl`/`2xl`/`display` for website section titles; defaults follow `level`.

allOf.description: The control that starts and stops a location trail, and the line that says one is running. Requires settings.tracking.enabled — without it the server refuses every call and the block does nothing. `record_id_expression` (usually "{{params.id}}" on a record's own page) names the record whose `geo` field the geofence is drawn around: arriving there fires a `location.arrived` workflow, leaving fires `location.departed`. Omit it for a plain trail with no fence. PUT IT ON THE PAGE THE WORK IS ON — a visit, a route, a delivery — never on a dashboard, and never on a page somebody leaves open all day.

searchable.description: Set false to withhold the table's search box. It otherwise appears once the list is long enough to be worth searching, and filters the loaded rows against what the cells show.

hidden_by_default.description: Start this column folded away. The reader can switch it on from the table's column picker, and the choice is remembered. Use it to keep a wide object's list scannable without dropping any of its fields.

oneOf.description: Action column: renders a button per row. on_click resolves {{row.id}} and {{row.data.<slug>}} from the current row at click time.

ask.description: Offers a box where the reader asks in their own words — «pedidos de más de 5.000 este mes» — and the phrase is compiled into the SAME filter grammar an author writes by hand. Nothing new reaches the database: the model picks among operators and fields that already exist, what it returns is validated before use, and the result is ANDed with the block's own filter, so it can only narrow. When a phrase cannot be compiled the table says so instead of quietly showing everything. The question lives in the URL, so it is shareable and the translation is cached.

icon.description: Optional emoji shown in the card corner.

compare.description: Optional comparison query (e.g. the previous period). When set the card shows the % change vs this value as a trend chip.

compare_window.description: Live compare for a dateless connected source: the runtime re-reads the tool with its window shifted back one span and shows the % change.

compare_label.description: Optional muted caption for the comparison, shown beside the trend chip (e.g. 'vs período anterior').

subtitle.description: Optional muted caption under the number naming its basis (e.g. 'promedio del periodo', 'acumulado en la ventana').

delta_good.description: Which direction of change is GOOD (green): 'up' (more is better) or 'down' (less is better, e.g. costs/churn).

variant.description: Tone of the card — drives its colour and default icon.

icon.description: Optional icon override (a Lucide name or an emoji); otherwise a default per variant is used.

metric.description: Optional highlighted figure shown large (e.g. '+34%'). For a LIVE figure use `compute` instead — it overrides this.

metric_label.description: Optional short caption under the big figure naming its unit/basis (e.g. 'semanas', 'pico retrasos'). Filter-safe: describes the number's KIND, never a value.

compute.description: Makes the card's figure LIVE: the runtime aggregates the data and shows the result as the metric, with a trend chip vs `compare`. Same shape as a stat block. Use it so an insight states a real, current number instead of a hand-written one.

compare.description: Optional comparison query (e.g. previous period) → drives the trend chip.

compare_window.description: Live compare for a dateless connected source: the runtime re-reads the tool with its window shifted back one span.

delta_good.description: Which direction of change is GOOD (green).

record_id_expression.description: Required when mode=edit. Expression resolving to the record id, e.g. {{params.id}}.

fill_from_document.description: Offers a «fill from a photo or PDF» button above the form: a vision model reads the document and fills the fields it can. It FILLS and never saves — the person checks every value and submits as usual, because a model reading a crumpled receipt in bad light is a suggestion and not a record. Fields the document does not clearly state are left empty on purpose, since somebody proof-reads what is filled in and not what is missing. Use it wherever a record is copied off a piece of paper: supplier invoices, receipts, delivery notes, meter readings, ID documents.

fill_from_voice.description: Offers a «dictate it» button above the form: the person records, the platform transcribes and reads the transcript for fields. Same rules as fill_from_document — it FILLS and never saves, never overwrites what somebody already typed, and leaves blank whatever was not clearly said. The transcript comes back and is shown, so a wrong field has the words that produced it beside it. Use it for hands-busy work: an inspector on a ladder, a driver at a gate, a technician with gloves on.

description.description: Optional sub-title shown below the title; also drives aria-describedby.

block_record_detail.description: Read-only view of ONE record's fields. Requires object_id, record_id_expression (resolves to the record id — e.g. {{params.id}} on a detail page, or {{row.id}}) and fields[] ({field_id, label_override?}). The detail half of a master-detail layout: pair it (e.g. in a split_view) with a table whose row action navigates with the id as a param.

presence.description: Shows who ELSE has this record open. Two people about to edit the same order is the thing worth knowing, and knowing it is what stops the second one wasting the work. It says somebody is HERE and never what they are doing.

block_record_activity.description: A record's history: the changes it went through and the comments people left on it, newest first, with a box for adding one. Requires record_id_expression (resolves to the record — e.g. {{params.id}}). Pair it with record_detail on a detail page. Reading needs the role's `read` on the object; commenting needs `update`.

block_related_list.description: A record's children: lists the records of another object that point back to THIS record via a relation. Requires object_id (the CHILD object to list), via_relation_field_id (a relation field ON the child object that points to the parent) and parent_id_expression (resolves to the parent id — e.g. {{params.id}} or {{row.id}}) plus columns[] ({field_id, label_override?}). Pair it with record_detail on a detail page (e.g. an Order's line items beneath the order).

oneOf.description: Action column: a button per row, exactly as on a table. on_click resolves {{row.id}} and {{row.data.<slug>}} from the clicked row. This is where a child record's own edit and delete live — a child object usually has no page of its own, so without it a line item can be added and never corrected.

block_data_grid.description: An editable table: record rows whose cells can be edited inline and saved (update_record) without leaving the page. Requires data_source ({object_id, filter?, sort?}) and columns[] ({field_id, label_override?, editable?}). Editable cells render a type-appropriate input (text, number, select, checkbox, date); computed fields (formula/lookup/rollup), relations and files are always read-only. Like `table` but writable — use `table` for read-only lists with row actions.

block_filter_bar.description: A row of page-level filter controls that drive {{params.*}}. Each control writes the user's input to a named URL query param; data blocks then react via a data_source.filter condition whose value_expression is "{{params.<name>}}" (an empty value is ignored, so the unfiltered set shows). Requires controls[] each {param (URL param name, snake_case), type (search|select|date_range), label?, placeholder? (search), options?, default?}. A `date_range` control renders preset window pills (Hoy/7d/30d/90d/Año/Todo by default; override with options[{value,label}]) and writes the preset KEY to the param; wire each block to react with a filter {op:"gte", field_id:<a date field>, value_expression:"{{range_start(default(params.<param>, '30d'))}}"} — range_start maps the key to the window-start date and 'all' clears it. Set `default` (e.g. "30d") to preselect a window.

default.description: Preselected value (e.g. a date_range preset key like "30d").

description.description: One executive line under the title saying what the chart shows and how to read it.

drill_param.description: Clicking a category toggles this page param (the category filter's), re-scoping the whole board — drill-down via the same wiring the select filter uses.

stacked.description: Stack marks cumulatively (part-to-whole) instead of overlaying them. With `series_field_id` it stacks the bar segments. With a COMBO `series` array where EVERY series is type 'area' (≥2 of them), it renders a STACKED AREA ("marea"): each series is a cumulative band and the Y axis spans the total — use it to show how categories compose a total over time (e.g. tickets by area stacked to the daily total). Ignored for a combo that mixes bar/line marks.

bucket.description: When the X / group_by field is a date or datetime (incl. sys_created_at), truncate it to this period so the chart shows one point per day/week/month/quarter/year (sorted chronologically) instead of one per timestamp. Defaults to 'day' for a date/datetime X; ignored for non-date fields.

series.description: COMBO chart: overlay several typed measures on one shared X axis (group_by_field_id, or x_field_id). When present, the chart renders as a combo and the top-level chart_type/aggregation/y_field_id are ignored (still set chart_type, e.g. 'bar', to satisfy the schema). Each series picks its own mark and which Y axis it uses — set axis:'right' for a measure on a different scale (DUAL AXIS), e.g. revenue (bar, left) + conversion rate (line, right). By default every series reads the chart's data_source object; a series may instead set its OWN data_source (+ group_by_field_id/x_field_id in that object) to overlay a measure from a DIFFERENT object on the same X — this is how you plot two separate connected objects that share an X (e.g. OTD by sale-date vs OTD by delivery-date) as two lines in one chart. Series align by their X VALUE, so the X fields must bucket to the same labels (same date bucket).

field_id.description: Numeric field for sum/avg/min/max (omit for count). Belongs to this series' object (its own data_source if set, else the chart's).

object_id.description: Shortcut to overlay a measure from a DIFFERENT object: set this series' object_id and its field_id, and it reads that object on the same X. When the object shares the chart's schema (e.g. OTD by sale-date vs delivery-date), the X field is mapped by slug automatically — you need not repeat group_by_field_id. Use `data_source` instead when the series needs its own filter.

data_source.description: Optional: read THIS series from a different object than the chart's, to overlay a measure from another connected/internal object on the same X. When set, this series' field_id and group_by_field_id/x_field_id must reference fields of THIS object. Prefer the simpler `object_id` shortcut unless the series needs its own filter. Omit both to read the chart's data_source.

group_by_field_id.description: Optional per-series X/category field, used when this series' object differs from the chart's AND does not share its slug. Usually unnecessary — the X is mapped by slug. Defaults to the chart's group_by_field_id/x_field_id.

x_field_id.description: Alias of group_by_field_id for this series (use either).

axis.description: Which Y axis this series is scaled against. 'right' is the secondary axis for a different unit/scale.

block_pivot.description: A 2-D matrix: rows x columns, each cell an aggregate. In `cohort` mode the columns become the period OFFSET from each row's own cohort (month 0, 1, 2...) and each cell is the % of that cohort still present - the retention table. Rows and columns may each be a date, bucketed by `bucket` / `column_bucket`; a date column left unbucketed makes every timestamp its own column.

bucket.description: Truncate the ROW field when it is a date/datetime. In cohort mode this is when the cohort was born (signup, first order).

column_bucket.description: Truncate the COLUMN field when it is a date/datetime. A cohort table needs this: in cohort mode this is the date of the activity being tracked.

mode.description: matrix: cells are the aggregate itself. cohort: columns become the offset from each row's own start and cells become the % of that cohort still present - a retention table.

eyebrow.description: Small uppercase label above the title (e.g. 'REPORTE OPERATIVO · YUHU'). Optional leading icon via eyebrow_icon.

eyebrow_icon.description: Optional icon name shown before the eyebrow label.

stat.description: An optional headline figure shown as a card floated in the hero (a live-resolved KPI). Mirrors a metric_grid item.

icon.description: An emoji (🌍) or a Lucide icon name.

field_id.description: Field whose values become words; each distinct value is sized by how often it occurs.

compare_window.description: Live compare for a dateless connected source: the runtime re-reads the tool with its window shifted back one span.

compare_label.description: Optional muted caption beside the trend chip (e.g. 'vs período anterior').

subtitle.description: Optional muted caption under the number naming its basis (e.g. 'promedio del periodo', 'acumulado en la ventana').

block_progress.description: Linear progress bar showing one aggregate against a max_value (the 100% mark). Same data shape as gauge but a horizontal bar — compact, and stacks cleanly in a column for several goals at once. Props: label, query, aggregation (count|sum|avg|min|max), field_id (required for non-count), max_value (required), format (number|currency|percentage), color (hex).

block_gantt.description: Horizontal schedule: one bar per record spanning start_field_id → end_field_id (both date/datetime), laid out on a shared time axis. Requires data_source, start_field_id, end_field_id and title_field_id (the bar label). Optional: label, color_field_id (single_select — colours each bar). Good for projects, leases, bookings — anything with a start and an end. Use calendar for single-date events and timeline for a chronological list.

left_fraction.description: 1-11; right takes 12 - left_fraction. Default 4 = 1/3 left, 2/3 right.

geo_field_id.description: A `geo` field carrying both halves of the point. Use this OR the lat/lng pair, not both.

block_barcode.description: Scannable codes, drawn from records — one per row, from the same data pipeline as every other block. A page filtered to one record prints one label; the same page unfiltered prints a sheet of them, which is what label stock is. Requires data_source and field_id (the value to encode). Optional: symbology (code128 default | ean13 | qr), caption_field_id (human-readable line under the code), show_text, height_px, per_row (how many across — match it to the label sheet). Pair it with a download_pdf action carrying a label paper size.

block_record_form.description: A form whose FIELDS COME FROM RECORDS instead of the manifest — one input per row returned by `questions`. This is what lets an app's own users define a questionnaire: HR writes the questions as data, and employees answer a real form rather than a spreadsheet. Use it for surveys, inspection checklists, audits and performance reviews. Each answer is written as its own record (so filters, charts, per-question aggregates and exports all work with the ordinary engine), grouped by one submission record. Requires questions, label_field_id, type_field_id, type_map and answers.

questions.description: Which records become the questions. Filter it to one questionnaire and sort it, because the order questions appear in is part of what somebody authored.

label_field_id.description: The field holding the question TEXT.

type_field_id.description: The field holding what KIND of answer this question wants, in the app's own vocabulary.

type_map.description: How that vocabulary maps to inputs: {"escala_1_5": "rating", "si_no": "boolean"}. The right-hand side is a field type (rating, slider, boolean, long_text, string, number, date, single_select). Anything unmapped renders as text rather than nothing.

options_field_id.description: For choice questions: a field holding the options, as an array or a newline/comma separated list.

required_field_id.description: A boolean field marking a question as required.

question_field_id.description: Relation on the answer pointing back at its question.

value_field_ids.description: Which column each kind of answer is written to: {"rating": "<numeric field>", "long_text": "<text field>"}. Separate columns rather than one, because a number stored as text cannot be averaged.

parent_field_id.description: Relation on the answer pointing at the submission that groups it.

submission.description: The record that groups one person's answers.

values.description: Field-slug → value map written on the submission, e.g. {"encuesta": "{{params.id}}"}.

completed_field_id.description: Optional. A string field on the submission object to stamp with when it was filed. COARSENED TO THE DATE when anonymous is true, because an exact time re-identifies as surely as a name — thirty people produce thirty distinct minutes. Omit it and nothing is stamped.

anonymous.description: The submission carries NO link to the person answering, and its timestamp is coarsened to the DATE — an exact time re-identifies somebody as surely as a name would. Pair it with `participation` to know who still has to answer without being able to read what anybody said. This is what makes a climate survey worth running: the moment employees suspect it is traceable, the answers stop meaning anything.

participation.description: Optional. Records that THIS person answered, in a separate object with no link to their answers — so somebody can be reminded without anybody being able to read what they said.

person_lookup.description: Optional. Send the questionnaire to a ROSTER the app keeps: find the row whose match_field_id holds the current user's id, and write THAT record's id into person_field_id (which must then be a relation to this object). Without it the marker carries the raw user id, which nothing can join against — so "who has not answered yet" is only expressible with this. Somebody absent from the roster is refused, rather than answering with no marker and being able to answer again tomorrow.

once.description: Default true: one filing per person. The marker is what makes this enforceable, so a questionnaire meant to be filed REPEATEDLY (a daily checklist, a shift inspection) must set false — or declare no participation at all. Scoped by whatever `values` puts on the marker, so one participation object can serve several questionnaires without them counting as each other.

icon.description: Optional emoji or named icon (list_available_icons); a sensible default per variant otherwise.

dismissible.description: Show a close button that hides the alert for the session.

src.description: Image URL. If omitted, initials from `name` are shown on an accent tile.

name.description: Used for the initials fallback and the image alt text.

label.description: Optional primary text shown beside the avatar.

caption.description: Optional secondary text under the label.

href.description: Optional link; the last item renders as the current page (no link).
Optional link the slide opens on click.

current_step.description: 0-based index of the active step; earlier steps render as done, later as upcoming.

variant.description: Colour preset. Use `color` for a custom hex instead.

block.description: A page block. Its `type` must be one of the catalog types (container, text, heading, divider, spacer, table, stat, form, lead_form, button, modal, chart, pivot, kanban, calendar, markdown, image, html, hero, feature_grid, cta, stat_band, insight, stepper, badge, alert, avatar, breadcrumb, carousel, testimonials, faq, pricing, word_cloud, flow, metric_grid, sparkline, gauge, heatmap, timeline, funnel, map, tabs, accordion, split_view, card_grid, multi_step_form). If this failed, the `type` is unknown or the block is missing a required prop for that type — call list_available_components for the catalog and each type's required props.

action.description: A single step inside an action_sequence (button.on_click, form.on_submit/on_cancel, table action column). Its `type` must be one of: navigate, open_modal, close_modal, create_record, update_record, delete_record, show_toast, refresh, run_workflow, scan_to_find, download_pdf, share, copy, speak, toggle_fullscreen, require_identity. If this failed, the action `type` is unknown or it is missing a required arg for that type — call list_available_actions for each action's required props and the canonical patterns.

oneOf.description: Scan a barcode with the camera, find the ONE record whose `field_id` holds that code, and open `page_slug` for it. `param` names the query parameter carrying the id (default "id"). Nothing happens if the sheet is closed; an unknown or ambiguous code says so and leaves the reader where they were, because navigating on a bad scan is how somebody ends up working on the wrong pallet. Signed-in runtime only. Use it for goods-in, stock checks, asset audits and picking: point the camera, get the record.

Download a PDF of one of this app's pages, rendered by a real browser so it looks like the screen. `page_slug` names the page; `params` scope it — {"id": "{{params.id}}"} on a record detail prints THAT record, and a filtered list prints the rows the reader is looking at. Use it for work orders, quotes, delivery notes and certificates: the person who needs the paper is usually the customer, who does not have the app.

paper.description: Named rather than measured, because label stock is SOLD by these names and a paper size out by two millimetres is a wasted roll. a4/letter are documents with margins; the label_* sizes print edge to edge — 4×6in shipping, 2×1in asset tags, 62×29mm Dymo address.

oneOf.description: Hand something to whatever the person shares things with — WhatsApp, mail, AirDrop. Give `page_slug` (with the same `params`/`paper` as download_pdf) to share that page's PDF as a FILE: that is how a signed delivery note reaches a customer who has no login and is never going to be given one. Otherwise it shares `text` + `url` (defaulting to the page the reader is on). Falls back to copying the link where there is no share sheet, and to the plain download when a file cannot be shared, so it is never a dead end. Signed-in runtime only for the PDF form.

Put text on the clipboard — a tracking number, a reference, a link somebody has to paste into another system. Interpolates {{row.*}}/{{params.*}}/{{form.*}}. Says whether it landed rather than claiming success blindly.

Say it out loud, for the half of a job done with both hands full: the next address on the route, the quantity to pick, the name at the door. Interpolates {{row.*}}/{{params.*}}/{{form.*}}. `lang` overrides the voice's language (defaults to the app's locale). A browser that cannot speak shows the words as a toast instead.

Ask the device WHO is holding it — the fingerprint, the face or the PIN it already knows — before the rest of the sequence runs. For the action somebody should have to mean: a refund, a write-off, a price override, a deletion that cannot be undone. A confirm dialog asks whether you meant it; this asks who you are. Put it FIRST in the sequence; it is checked server-side against a challenge this server minted, and nothing else in the sequence runs if it fails. Never queued offline — an approval is a statement about a moment, and replaying one six hours later against whatever the record has become is the failure it exists to prevent. A device with no sensor, or a refused prompt, stops the sequence and says so, so do not gate an action people must be able to take on any machine.

Go full screen, or come back out. For the app running on a tablet bolted to a counter: the browser chrome above it is an escape hatch into the rest of the internet, and a till that can be navigated away from is a till that will be. Needs a tap, which is why it is a button action and not a page setting.

Open a modal block by id. Optional `params` are injected as the modal's local context — read inside the modal's child blocks with {{params.<key>}}, including the form's record_id_expression for an Edit modal that needs the row id.

params.description: Optional key→value map. Values can be expression strings ({{row.id}}, {{form.x}}) or literal scalars. Each key becomes available inside the modal as {{params.<key>}}.

values.description: Field-slug → value map, and the WHOLE payload written — nothing merges the form's own fields into it, so a required field missing here is refused on every submit. Values can be expression strings ({{form.x}}, {{row.id}}, {{current_user.id}}) OR literal scalars (true, 42, "open", null). RecordWriteService casts them to the field's type on save. Two things this map must not do: fill a RELATION with {{current_user.id}} (that is the platform user id, never a record id — use {{form.<slug>}}, or {{current_user.email}} against the target's email field), and overwrite a field the same form renders (whatever the person chose is then discarded).

Field-slug → value map, and the WHOLE payload written — nothing merges the form's own fields into it, so a required field missing here is refused on every submit. Values can be expression strings ({{form.x}}, {{row.id}}, {{current_user.id}}) OR literal scalars (true, 42, "open", null). RecordWriteService casts them to the field's type on save. Two things this map must not do: fill a RELATION with {{current_user.id}} (that is the platform user id, never a record id — use {{form.<slug>}}, or {{current_user.email}} against the target's email field), and overwrite a field the same form renders (whatever the person chose is then discarded).

oneOf.description: Show a toast notification. Required keys: `type`:"show_toast" and `message` (the text to show — NOT `text`). Optional `level` (info|success|warning|error).

trigger.description: A workflow trigger. Its `type` must be one of: manual, record.created, record.updated, record.deleted, location.arrived, location.departed, schedule, webhook.inbound. If this failed, the trigger `type` is unknown or it is missing a required arg for that type (record.* needs object_id; schedule needs cron) — call list_available_triggers for each trigger's required props.

oneOf.description: Fires when somebody RECORDING THEIR ROUTE crosses the fence drawn around this record's `geo` field — arriving, or leaving. Needs settings.tracking.enabled and a `tracking` block on the page the person is on; nothing fires for somebody who never started a trail, which is the point. Payload: the record, plus {location: {lat, lng, distance_m}}. Use it to stamp a visit's arrival, tell a customer the technician is outside, or close a route step. Never fires for the state a trail STARTED in: somebody who opens the app already at the site has not arrived while it was watching.

Fires when a record's date/datetime field, shifted by `offset`, reaches now — e.g. 3 days before an invoice due_date. field_id must be a date or datetime field on the object. `at` (HH:MM, default 09:00) and `timezone` (IANA, default UTC) anchor date-only fields. Optional `filter` narrows which records qualify.

Fires when an inbound message arrives on a chat channel (WhatsApp or web widget). `channel_id` binds the workflow to a specific channel in your organization. Optional `contains` fires only when the message text contains that substring (case-insensitive). Trigger payload: {channel:{id,type,name}, message:{text,content_type}, contact:{id,name,identifier}, conversation_id}.

Fires when a bot hands a conversation to a person (a `human_handoff` node with notify on). `channel_id` binds the workflow to a specific channel in your organization. This is how a team gets told: send an email, post to Slack, create a ticket record. Trigger payload: {channel:{id,type,name}, chatbot:{id,name}, conversation_id, reason, mode, contact:{id,name,email,identifier}}.

Fires when a third-party provider POSTs to the integration's signed webhook URL (one URL per integration, set the provider's signing secret on the Integration). `integration_id` binds the workflow to that integration; optional `event` fires only for that event type (e.g. a GitHub X-GitHub-Event header or a Stripe body `type`). Trigger payload: {integration_id, event, body, headers}.

Polls a connected tool (a rest_api/graphql action that returns a list) every `interval_minutes` and fires once per item not seen before — for providers without webhooks. `tool_id` is the connected action; `items_path` is the dot-path to the array in the response (omit if the response IS the array); `watermark_path` is a monotonic field on each item (e.g. id or created_at) used to detect new items. Trigger payload: {tool_id, item, watermark}.

Fires when an inbound-email provider (Postmark/Mailgun/SendGrid/…) POSTs a parsed email to the integration's email webhook URL. `integration_id` binds the workflow to that integration (set its provider + signing secret/token there). Optional `to_contains`/`subject_contains` narrow which emails fire (case-insensitive). The payload is normalised across providers. Trigger payload: {integration_id, email:{from,from_name,to,subject,text,html,message_id}}.

step.description: A workflow step. Its `type` must be one of: record.create, record.update, record.delete, record.query, record.aggregate, set_variable, log, branch, foreach, ai.complete, agent.invoke, http.request, script.run, connector.call. If this failed, the step `type` is unknown or it is missing a required arg for that type — call list_available_steps for each step's required props and the canonical patterns.

value.description: Literal or expression — resolved before assignment.

allOf.description: Tell a person something happened. `channel` email sends a branded message; in_app raises a notification in the app's bell; push reaches the phone while the app is CLOSED, which is the only one that finds somebody who is driving. Bounded per organization per hour — this is an outbound channel a record write can reach.

to.description: Destinations. Each is an email address, `user:<id>`, `role:<app role slug>` (everyone granted that role in the Access panel) or `owner`. Expressions are resolved first, so "{{trigger.record.data.email}}" works.

link.description: Optional URL the message links to (a page of this app, or an absolute link).

items.description: Expression resolving to an array, e.g. {{steps.calc.output.primes}}. The sub-steps run once per element.

item_variable.description: Variable name the current element is bound to (default 'item'), referenced via {{vars.<name>}}.

index_variable.description: Optional variable bound to the 0-based index.

agent_id.description: Id of the Sapiensly agent to invoke. Unlike ai.complete (a bare prompt), this runs the configured agent with its own model, instructions, knowledge bases (RAG) and tools. Use list_agents to get a real id — never invent one.

message.description: The input/prompt sent to the agent, resolved against the workflow context. The reply is addressable via {{steps.<id>.output.text}}.

code.description: JavaScript run in an isolated QuickJS sandbox (no network/filesystem/host access). Receives the resolved `input` map as the `input` argument; whatever it `return`s becomes the step output.

input.description: Map of name → expression resolved against the workflow context before the script runs.

tool_id.description: Id of the configured connector action (a REST/GraphQL/database Tool). Use list_connector_actions to get a real id and its typed inputs — never invent one.

inputs.description: Map of the action's input name → expression resolved against the workflow context. Outputs are addressable via {{steps.<id>.output.data.…}}.

access_mode.description: How org members reach this app. 'open' (default): every member who can see the app gets the default role; assignments only elevate. 'allowlist': only members with an explicit role assignment may use the app; everyone else is denied entry.

public.description: Opens this app as a PUBLIC PORTAL: anyone on the internet, with no account, reaches it at /a/{public_slug} once published. access_mode above governs org members; this governs strangers, and it is deny-by-default — a visitor sees ONLY what page_policies and object_policies grant to role_id explicitly. An object or page with no policy is invisible to them, the inverse of the member default.

enabled.description: Whether the portal is open. Publishing is still a separate, explicit act — this alone does not put the app online.

role_id.description: The role an anonymous visitor assumes. Must be a declared role, and must NOT be the is_default role — the role members fall back to is not the role to hand the internet.

allow_writes.description: Whether visitors may submit data (forms, record actions). False (default) makes the portal read-only whatever the object policies say. When true, each write is still gated by the create/update/delete actions granted to role_id.

signup.description: Whether visitors can have an IDENTITY. 'none' (default): the portal is anonymous, so {{current_user.id}} resolves to null and a row_filter written against it matches nothing. 'open': anyone may sign in with a magic link sent to their address — what a self-service tracker or request form needs. 'invite': only addresses the organization added beforehand can sign in. Signing in is what makes 'each customer sees only their own rows' expressible.

member_role_id.description: The role a SIGNED-IN portal user assumes, when it should differ from the anonymous one. Omit and they keep role_id. This is how a portal shows a stranger a sign-in page and a customer their own orders.

tracking.description: Whether this app may record where its users GO. OFF unless it is here and enabled:true — the reverse of `offline`, and for the reverse reason: an app that stops working in a basement is broken, an app that follows people who did not agree is an incident. Even then nothing is recorded until the person taps start on a `tracking` block, a visible bar runs the whole time, and they can stop it. The web has no background geolocation, so a trail only exists while the app is open on screen — pair the page with keep_awake and expect gaps, which are recorded AS gaps. SET THIS ONLY when the brief asks for routes, arrival times or automatic check-in, say in your reply that you turned it on, and prefer the geofence (a `location.arrived` workflow) over the trail: knowing somebody arrived is what the business needs, and the breadcrumb trail is the part that feels like surveillance.

min_interval_s.description: Never record two points closer together in time than this (default 30). Lower is not better: it flattens a battery and fills a table with rows saying the same thing.

min_distance_m.description: …or closer together in space (default 50). Standing still should cost nothing.

geofence_radius_m.description: How close counts as arrived (default 150). Below about fifty metres a fence is narrower than a phone's own fix and fires on somebody standing still.

retain_days.description: How long a trail is kept before it is deleted (default 30). This is the promise that a trail does not outlive the work it documents — set it to the shortest span that still answers the question the app was built to answer.

offline.description: What this app may leave on a device. A built app works without a signal by default — pages it has seen are cached, and writes made offline (with their photos and signatures) are held until the signal returns. The cost is that tenant rows sit on a phone's disk in the clear. For a work order that is the right trade; for a payroll run it is not. Set enabled:false to turn it off for this app, or list objects under exclude_objects to keep just those off the device. Omit this entirely unless the app handles data that must not leave the server.

enabled.description: Whether this app may be cached and used offline at all. Default true.

exclude_objects.description: Object SLUGS whose data must never be written to a device. A page is served no-store and never cached if ANYTHING on it reads one of them, and a write touching one is refused rather than queued — the person is told it needs a connection instead of being told it was saved.

density.description: The vertical rhythm of the app's surfaces. `compact` tightens rows and fields — the same type at a closer spacing — for lists people work through all day. Dashboards want `comfortable`.

theme.description: Color palette applied to the runtime: 'light' (default, clean white page) or 'dark' (dark surfaces).

accent.description: Brand accent colour (hex). Drives buttons, links and highlights across the app so everything looks cohesive. Set one per site.

palette_mode.description: Chart palette source: brand = cohesive categorical series from the accent (default); accent = monochromatic ramp of the accent; grays = neutral grayscale.

font.description: Body/heading font family family: sans (modern), serif (editorial), rounded (friendly), mono (technical).

fonts.description: Extra web-font families for this app's pages, loaded from the privacy-friendly Google Fonts mirror (fonts.bunny.net) — ANY Google Fonts family works. Each entry: "Family Name" or "Family Name:400,700,400i" (comma-separated weights, i = italic; omit for the default weight). Reach for this when the curated self-hosted catalog doesn't carry the voice the intent needs, then reference the family BY NAME in custom_css with a generic fallback (font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif). Prefer 1-2 families with explicit weights — every family+weight adds page weight.

languages.description: The languages a LANDING is served in, most important first. The FIRST entry is the default — the language every block's `content` is written in — and the others are the ones blocks may translate into via content_i18n. Fewer than two entries means a single-language landing and nothing is negotiated. On the public page the language is chosen SERVER-side (the page ships no JavaScript and cannot choose for itself): an explicit ?lang= wins, then the visitor's remembered choice, then the browser's Accept-Language, then the default. Each language gets its own URL (?lang=xx) so a link is shareable and both versions can be indexed.

seo_i18n.description: Per-language <head> metadata, keyed by language code — the title and description a person and a crawler read. settings.seo holds the default language; a language missing here falls back to it. Only makes sense alongside settings.languages.

navigation_layout.description: App chrome: 'top' (default) is a horizontal header bar — best for a few pages; 'sidebar' is a left navigation rail — best when the menu grows or needs nested groups. The sidebar renders `navigation.items` (which support nested `children`), falling back to the flat page list when no navigation is defined. Ignored when `surface` is 'landing' (a landing renders chrome-less).

surface.description: Explicit product surface, overriding content-based classification. 'landing' renders a public, chrome-less full-bleed page — no site header/sidebar/footer, so the page brings its own navbar/footer section blocks and each section paints itself edge to edge. Omit to let the app be classified from its blocks (app vs dashboard).

chatbot.description: Puts one of the organization's chatbots on this landing as a floating bubble. LANDING SURFACE ONLY, and the chatbot must belong to the same owner as the app — both are enforced by the validator. Reference the chatbot BY ID (list_chatbots); never paste the embed <script> into an html block, which silently does nothing because the page renders that markup without executing scripts. The bubble inherits this page's accent and typography at render time, so it reads as part of the design rather than bolted on. Omit ⇒ no chatbot.

id.description: The chatbot's id (chatbot_…), from list_chatbots. Must be active and owned by this app's organization. Note this is NOT a manifest id: it names a row outside the manifest, so it carries the platform's own 'chatbot_' prefix rather than the short in-manifest id shape.

position.description: Which bottom corner the bubble sits in. Use 'left' when the right corner already carries a CTA the page needs unobstructed.

greeting.description: Opening line the bubble shows before the visitor types. Write it in the page's own voice — it is the first thing a visitor reads from the bot. Omit to use the chatbot's own configured greeting.

seo.description: Head metadata for the public landing page. Falls back to the app's name/description when unset — but a real landing ALWAYS authors these: the title/description are what shows up in search results and link previews.

title.description: The <title> / og:title — the search-result headline (~60 chars ideal).

description.description: The meta description / og:description — the search-result snippet (~155 chars ideal).

og_image.description: Absolute URL of the social-share image (og:image, ~1200×630).

custom_css.description: Advanced ESCAPE HATCH: raw CSS for fine visual tweaks beyond accent/font/theme/block-style. Budget: up to 20,000 chars — except a landing surface (settings.surface="landing"), whose bespoke look IS its CSS, which may use up to 60,000. It is AUTOMATICALLY SCOPED to this app's surface (wrapped in `.sp-app-surface { … }` via CSS nesting) so it can NEVER affect the Sapiensly platform or another app — write plain selectors like `.card { … }` (no need to add the scope yourself; selectors only match inside this app). Prefer the design tokens (var(--sp-accent), var(--sp-accent-blue)) and the per-block `style` first; reach for custom_css only for what they can't express. FORBIDDEN (rejected at save): @import, <style>/<script> tags, javascript: URLs, expression(). Don't hide the header/nav (it holds the exit) and keep text/background contrast readable. See framework_reference topic=custom_css.

brand.description: Site identity shown in the header.

logo_dark.description: Optional logo variant for DARK surfaces (a light-ink logo for dark backgrounds). The runtime picks it by the active theme and falls back to `logo` when unset. Inherited from the org Brandbook's dark logo.

icon.description: Optional square brand icon shown when the sidebar layout is collapsed — an emoji, a named icon, or an image URL. Inherited from the org Brandbook's icon when unset.

icon_dark.description: Optional square brand icon variant for DARK surfaces. Falls back to `icon` when unset. Inherited from the org Brandbook's dark icon.

header_bg.description: Optional background colour (hex) for the site header bar that holds the logo + main menu. Header text auto-picks a readable contrast. Inherited from the org Brandbook's 'Logo bg color' when unset.

derived_rate.description: PROVEN from the sampled rows: this field's value equals numerator (minus minus_field_id, when set) divided by denominator, on every row. It is therefore NOT averageable: the mean of per-row rates weights a small row like a big one, which is a different number, not an approximation. Any block that aggregates this field must express it as a ratio (aggregation sum on the numerator, plus ratio_denominator sum on the denominator). When minus_field_id is set the numerator is a DIFFERENCE, which ratio_denominator cannot point at, so no KPI can state that rate honestly: do not put the field in a stat, metric_grid, gauge or hero.
